chunks: From him, from one of our companions, raising it, said:
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Carry yourself for yourself, for if you do not do so, others will not carry you.'
ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about personal responsibility and carrying one's own burden?
ai.summary: In the context of al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) underscores the principle of individual accountability (*mas'uliyya*) within Shia jurisprudence, where one's spiritual burden cannot be transferred. It serves as a foundational reminder that while intercession exists, the primary responsibility for carrying the weight of one's deeds rests solely on the individual, highlighting the necessity of proactive self-discipline in the path to salvation. This teaching aligns with the broader Shia emphasis on personal agency in worship and moral conduct, distinguishing it from passive reliance on others' piety.

en.hubeali: From him, from one of our companions, raising it, said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Carry yourself (your burden) by yourself, for it you do not do so, others will not carry you’.
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from certain individuals of our people in a marfu’ manner who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Hold your soul responsible for yourself. If you did not do so others will not do for you.’”
